discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental demonstration of anyonic (fractional) exchange statistics of quasiparticles in the fractional quantum Hall effect

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'Ecole Normale Supérieure, Paris, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics / topological quantum matter
motivation: Quantum mechanics in two dimensions allows particles that are neither bosons nor fermions. Halperin showed in 1984 that fractional quantum Hall quasiparticles must obey such fractional exchange statistics, and his hierarchy and edge-state theory made anyons a concrete, testable property of real electronic matter. For four decades a direct observation was out of reach. In 2020 Fève and coworkers used an anyon 'collider', in which fractional quasiparticles meet at a beam splitter, and saw the cross-correlation signature of anyonic statistics. In the same year Manfra and coworkers, in exceptionally clean heterostructures, directly observed the braiding phase in a Fabry-Pérot interferometer. Later interferometry at other filling fractions confirmed these results. Together the theory and experiments establish a new kind of quantum statistics in nature, which changes how we teach identical particles and underpins topological quantum computation.
